Entries.Text: Views, paints and checks the navigation data of a loaded Dark Souls II map: the map's .ngp file, with one navmesh per MSB navmesh part, the gates where navmeshes meet and the gate graph enemies path through. Start in the Overlay tab, which draws it in the viewport; the other tabs work on what it draws.
Map {0} has no .ngp file.
Draws the map's navmeshes over the viewport, placed by the map offset as the game places them.
A click chooses the gate nearest it.
Flags

Draws the navmeshes: faces coloured by their flags (or one part of them), inner and open edges, the edges gates use, the gate points and the gate graph's links. The legend names what each colour means; Use paints with it.

Picks faces and paints their flags: the level (which enemy sizes may use the face), the type (ground, door, ladder, rope, drop, event area, water) and the attributes (blocked, door closed). Each paint stroke is one undoable edit. Flags change no geometry, so nothing else in the file changes.
Lists the map's gates: where two navmeshes share boundary edges, and the links between the gates of each navmesh, which enemies path through. Gates come from the geometry and are only shown here.
Checks the .ngp against the rules the game files keep, and compares the issues with the vanilla file, so only what the project changed stands out.
Only the picked navmesh
Draws and picks only the navmesh of the picked face.

Open edges
Boundary edges no gate uses: enemies can't leave the navmesh there.
Gate edges
Boundary edges a gate uses, where enemies cross into another navmesh.
Gate points
Each gate's point (the middle of its first edge), as a cross.
Gate links
The gate graph: a line between each two gates of the same navmesh, which enemies path along.

An enemy uses a face only if the face's level is greater than its own. The enemy's level is its weight type minus one (CHR_COMMON_PARAM weightType, likely), so 7 lets every enemy through and lower levels keep out bigger ones.

Ground
Ordinary ground: every enemy the level admits may walk it.
Door approach
Small faces beside doors, walked like ground. Inferred from where the game's faces lie.
Door threshold
The faces under a door. The door object finds them by this type and marks them closed (attribute Door closed) or locked (Blocked); enemies without useDoor (LOGIC_COM_PARAM) can't pass a closed door.
Ladder landing
Small faces at the ends of ladders, walked like ground. Inferred from where the game's faces lie.
Ladder
The vertical faces up a ladder. Only enemies with useLadder (LOGIC_COM_PARAM) climb them, up or down; none can stand on them.
Rope end
Crossed but not stood on. Inferred from where the game's few faces lie (next to rope faces).
Rope
Only enemies with useRope (LOGIC_COM_PARAM) cross these faces; none can stand on them.
Type 0x38
No game file uses it; walked like ground.
One-way drop
A steep edge enemies jump down but never climb up.
Event area
Faces a general location event (Navigation Mesh Change) finds in its shape by this type; scripts block and open them with the Blocked attribute.
Type 0x50
Walked like ground; found in Earthen Peak and Shaded Woods, perhaps poison. Its use is unknown.
Water
Walked like ground; found in shallow water (Shrine of Amana, Doors of Pharros, Shulva). Inferred from where the game's faces lie.

Blocked

No enemy may use the face. Doors set it while locked, fog walls while active, and event scripts (AddNavimeshAttribute / DeleteNavimeshAttribute, value 2) to close and open barriers. Set it here for a barrier that starts closed.
Door closed
On a door threshold, only enemies with useDoor may pass. Door objects set and clear it as they close and open; no game file stores it.
Closed door passable
On a closed door threshold, lets every enemy through. Some doors set it when they load; no game file stores it.

Rebuild

Rebuilds what follows from the geometry: the edges, half-edges, bounding box and face tree of the chosen navmeshes, and the gates, gate links and IDs of the whole map. Gates between two navmeshes not rebuilt are kept as they are.
Rebuild Picked Navmesh
Rebuilds the picked face's navmesh and the gates with its neighbours. One undoable edit.
Rebuild All

Rebuilds every navmesh and every gate. The face trees come out different from the game's (valid, but not built by the same rule), and 144 vanilla navmeshes whose edges the game tool welded get plain edge tables. One undoable edit.
The rebuild gives the same file: nothing to change.

Moves navmesh vertices with a brush (Raise, Lower, Drag, Smooth). Edits show in the overlay until committed, which rebuilds the moved navmeshes' bounding boxes and face trees and the map's gates as one undoable edit. Keep Linked on near gates: an edge that moves away from its neighbour's loses its gate.
Writes the moved vertices into the .ngp: the moved navmeshes' bounding boxes and face trees, and the map's gates, links and IDs, are rebuilt. One undoable edit.
Other navmeshes' vertices under the brush move too, by the same falloff, so the edges two navmeshes share (their gates) stay joined.

Lists the map's navmeshes: each MSB navmesh part and the .ngp mesh of the same position. Generate makes a new navmesh (or replaces the chosen one) from the selected collision parts; Duplicate copies one moved by an offset; Remove takes one out with its part. Ladder adds a ladder at the selected ladder objects; Drop adds a one-way drop from the ledge nearest the picked point to the floor below. Gates, links and IDs follow. Each is one undoable edit.

Ladder

Adds a ladder at each selected ladder object, as the game's own ladders are made: a column of vertical Ladder faces 0.70 m wide at the object's position, facing its +Z, with a 0.70 m square Ladder landing at each end. The bottom landing lies behind the object on the floor at its foot; the top one lies ahead of it on the floor near the top of its bounds. Both are cut into those floors so enemies can step on and off. The ladder goes into the bottom floor's navmesh; a top floor in another navmesh meets the ladder through a gate.

Drop

Adds a One-way drop from a ledge to the floor below, as the game's own drops are made: steep faces joining the ledge's open edge to the floor beneath it, so enemies jump down but don't climb up. The ledge is the open edge of the picked navmesh nearest the picked point. The floor is found below the ledge, at a wall's foot or the run out from it; the drop's bottom is cut into it.

Pick a face beside a ledge first (Flags tab, Pick): the drop starts at its navmesh's nearest open edge.
Run
How far out from the ledge the drop lands, in metres. A wall's foot nearer than this is used instead. Vanilla drops slope 65° on average: about 0.5 m out for each metre down.
Highest
The highest drop, in metres: floors further below are ignored. The lowest is 0.5 m.
Add Drop
